newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines plans to increase sugar tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Philippines plans to increase sugar tariffs.

text.p: A Philippine committee formed by President Fidel Ramos to address the country's sugar glut recommended an increase in the tariff rate on imported sugar, the Presidential Palace said in a statement on Wednesday.

Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero had requested Tariff Commission chairman Emmanuel Velasco to increase the tariff to 133 percent from 100 percent from January 1 to June 30, 1997, and to 110 percent from 80 percent from July 1 to August 31, 1997, the statement said.
The proposed tariff increase on sugar importation did not cover compulsory purchases under World Trade Organisation rules, which are pegged this year at 43,000 tonnes, it said.
"With the increase in tariff, we are expecting that sugar importation will no longer be a lucrative business, which will be for the good of our local sugar industry," Escudero said.

"Hopefully it will work. In case it will not work in the expected magnitude, the task force is continuing its regular consultation with the local sugar producers and other leaders of the industry," Escudero added.

Escudero said the sugar task force, headed by Executive Secretary Ruben Torres, recommended that the country invoke the special safeguard provision under the WTO agreement due to repercussions suffered by local sugar farmers after cheaper imported sugar flooded the market.
"By consensus, it was agreed that we will invoke the SSP in the WTO agreement as an internal and temporary measure to save the local sugar industry," Escudero said.
Once the committee's recommendation is formally approved by the Cabinet, the government will formally notify the WTO, the statement said.
The Philippines has committed itself to cutting tariffs but the local sugar industry supports 400,000 sugar workers and political pressure to protect them has been building up.
